verdict.rationale: Weave's own docs say decorating functions with weave.op produces a nested trace tree, and Threads group traces belonging to a single session or conversation. It also documents sessions, turns, steps, tools and sub-agents as first-class concepts, with automatic tracing for agent SDKs and wrappers (start_conversation, start_turn, start_tool) for custom agent loops. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of nested agent spans and session grouping.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace multi-step agent runs as nested spans grouped into sessions or threads

citations.quote: Decorate all the functions you want to trace, this will generate a trace tree of the inputs and outputs of all your functions
Threads are collections of Traces related to a single session or conversation.
Weave now brings sessions, turns, steps, tools, and sub-agents as first-class concepts, making it much easier to navigate an agent session the way the agent actually executed it.
Custom agents — wrap your own loop with `start_conversation`, `start_turn`, `start_llm`, and `start_tool`.
Trace agents. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls show up in the Agents tab.
